::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
China's first 'CIDM' (collaborative IDM) project — pooling IC-design firms, end-application companies, and the manufacturer as joint investors — founded by Richard Chang (Zhang Rujing), who also founded SMIC. Domestic reporting in 2026 describes Zhang as having since departed the company he founded, citing difficulty retaining talent — a leadership change this tracker has not independently corroborated beyond that single report. By 2026, reported capacity stood at roughly 60,000 wafers/month (8-inch line) and 40,000 wafers/month (12-inch line), with an annual output value around ¥4.6 billion at full capacity. SiEn was added to the US Commerce Department's Entity List on December 2, 2024, as part of the 140-entity semiconductor package — one of only a handful of wafer fabs directly listed in that round.
:::

**Chinese name:** 芯恩（青岛）集成电路 (Xīn'ēn (Qīngdǎo) Jíchéng Diànlù)

## What does this facility make?

Logic/foundry, analog/power, and RF/wireless chips at 28nm and 40nm on both 200mm and 300mm wafers.

## Why does it matter?

A structurally different ownership model (collaborative IDM, not a pure foundry or a single-owner state fab) from every other entry in this tracker, and notable for its founder's direct SMIC lineage. In September 2026 it opened a separate 'Industry Innovation Center' — five R&D buildings on a 30,154 sq m site, explicitly a research/innovation facility rather than a new wafer production line — framed domestically as a shift from 'scale manufacturing to innovation creation.'

## Project Timeline

- **Apr 2018** — SiEn (Qingdao) established in the Qingdao West Coast New Area (Huangdao)
- **Jan 2021** — Production commences on the first-phase lines
- **Sep 2026** — Breaks ground on the SiEn Industry Innovation Center, a five-building R&D complex (not a new fab line) in the Qingdao Free Trade Zone IC industrial park
